.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (Known false positives: 'One criterion covering a whole flow'; severity anchors)
qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md (independent credit, positive controls, 'Reuse an observed fact, not another row's pass flag')
qc/runs/kittle-2026-10-09-r3/raw-evidence-index.json (scope header only: golden scripted observations; no weak-app discrimination runs)
evidence: No incompatible products found: I walked the shared-database order of all 16 functional criteria against seed_data.json (e.g. timer_changes shortens M-13 to 7 days at 2026-05-12, deleting only K-13 (05-04); 'Draft will sent for your review.' (K-8, 05-10) used later by message_links/live_updates and the held executor K-7 survive; persistence restores M-12 timer and Sian's M-11 wall). Gate-vs-scored overlaps are zero-weight gates (scoring.toml [gates] render=0.0, constraints=0.0), not double scoring. Most positive controls are justified per REVIEW_POLICY ('A negative needs a successful control'). However the persistence criterion re-grades the existence of features already scored in their own criteria instead of grading restart-equality against a before-restart baseline - exactly the double-penalty pattern Colderwater lesson 16 records as a portal row-28 flag. tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:256-261: setup 'a. ... edit JUDGE-S0 ..., place a hold on JUDGE-S1 ...' and 'b. Set M-12's timer to 30 days, and wall sian@kittle.test from M-11' are performed but NOT observed before restart (only step c notes searches and Dev's unread count, which leg 4 / leg 3 grade baseline-relative, correctly). Leg 1 (line 261) then requires 'Harriet can open its earlier version' (also graded by edits_and_stale_edit leg 1, line 162, and timer_changes positive control, line 129) and 'JUDGE-S1 is On hold' (hold mark display, graded by hold_scope_and_release leg 2, line 146); leg 3 (line 263) requires 'M-12 shows 30 days' (timer control + label, graded by timer_changes leg 1, line 130) and 'Sian gets not-available for M-11' (wall-adding control, graded by wall_added_live, lines 83-88). So a missing UI feature fails persistence (weight 2.0) in addition to its own criterion, even if storage survives restart perfectly. The comment at judge.toml:35 'Each observable is graded in exactly one criterion' is therefore not true. Secondary duplicate: timer_changes leg 1 (line 130) 'the held executor message stays marked On hold' re-grades the thread hold mark (hold_scope_and_release leg 2) when its own observable is only that the held message survives shortening (its Fails-if line 135 says 'if the held message is deleted'); under the prompt rule 'Every numbered leg ... must hold' (prompt.md:26) the mark leg still fails it. Notes (not blocking): wall_mentions_and_links (line 72, 'Harriet's preview or link did not work' fails) and message_links (line 189) both grade preview+follow-link, but the former is a needed positive control for the wall leg in individual mode; polish phone_matter vs visual phone_chambers (overflow/box reachable at 390 px), polish hold_mark vs visual retention_marks, and polish transcript_print vs functional search_and_transcript B2 are correlated binary-presence vs likert-craft grades of different grain, acceptable per skill but worth watching. Raw evidence index contains only golden scripted observations; no weak-app reward run measured the cascade, so impact is derived from criterion text.
counterexample: Weak-but-durable app: stores everything in SQLite and survives restart perfectly, enforces holds server-side (delete refused), but its UI has no 'earlier versions' viewer and shows the hold only as a tooltip-less internal flag (no On hold mark). It correctly fails edits_and_stale_edit (1.5), hold_scope_and_release (2.0) and timer_changes' positive control (2.0), and then ALSO fails persistence (2.0) via leg 1 ('Harriet can open its earlier version', 'JUDGE-S1 is On hold') although nothing was lost across the restart. Likewise an app with no wall-adding control fails wall_added_live and persistence leg 3 ('Sian gets not-available for M-11'). Conversely an app with a working hold mark but no hold persistence is graded fairly; the defect is the one-way double penalty. A smaller instance: an app whose held executor message correctly survives the 7-day shortening but whose thread lacks a hold badge fails timer_changes leg 1 as well as hold_scope_and_release.
suggested_fix: In persistence, record each set-up state before restart (edited mark + earlier version text, JUDGE-S1 hold mark, M-12 timer label, Sian's M-11 not-available) and grade only that each observed state is unchanged after restart_app, stating that a state which never took effect before the restart is scored elsewhere (keep posting/reply/delete as the positive control); and reword timer_changes leg 1 to 'the held executor message stays' (hold mark scored in hold_scope_and_release).
